item.title: Nine more children die with measles symptoms
item.description:
Nine more children died with measles symptoms in the 24 hours until 8am on Tuesday, while 1,351 suspected and confirmed cases were reported across the country, the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) said.
With the latest fatalities, the number of deaths from suspected measles has risen to 1,256 since March 15. No deaths from confirmed measles were reported during the latest 24-hour period, keeping the confirmed death toll at 105.
The combined death toll from confirmed measles and measles-like symptoms has now reached 1,361 since March 15.
The DGHS said 1,283 suspected cases and 68 confirmed cases were reported in the 24 hours until 8am Tuesday.
Since March 15, the country has recorded 259,190 suspected cases and 26,300 confirmed cases, according to the latest DGHS data.
A total of 231,999 patients with suspected measles have been admitted to hospitals nationwide since March 15. Of them, 223,158 have been discharged, the release added.

item.title: Govt plans 3,000 electric buses to overhaul Dhaka’s public transport
item.description:
The government plans to introduce 3,000 modern, environment-friendly electric buses in phases to bring discipline to Dhaka’s chaotic public transport system, improve passenger services and reduce air pollution.
The initiative will initially be launched under government management through the Bangladesh Road Transport Corporation (BRTC), with plans to gradually bring private bus operators under the new system.
The plan was announced at a meeting on public transport reform and implementation of the "gross-cost" model under the World Bank-funded Bangladesh Clean Air Project (BCAP) at the Road Transport and Bridges Ministry on Tuesday.
Road Transport, Railways and Shipping Minister Shaikh Rabiul Alam chaired the meeting.
The minister said the government aims to make Dhaka’s public transport system modern, safe, affordable and passenger-friendly through the phased introduction of 3,000 electric buses.
He said merely increasing the number of buses would not resolve the problems, stressing the need for structural changes to the existing operational system.
The transformation could take two to three years, with World Bank support.
Under the proposed gross-cost model, buses will operate through tripartite agreements involving the Dhaka Transport Coordination Authority (DTCA), bus operators and vehicle suppliers, replacing the conventional route-permit-based system.
Fares collected from passengers will be deposited with the authorities, which will pay operators at a fixed rate per kilometre based on compliance with prescribed service standards, rather than passenger numbers or fare collections.
The model is expected to reduce unhealthy competition among buses for passengers, ensure adherence to schedules and improve transparency and accountability in operations.
The introduction of electric buses is also expected to reduce vehicle emissions and improve air quality.
However, the initiative will require charging infrastructure, maintenance facilities, skilled manpower, route restructuring and effective monitoring.
State Minister for Road Transport and Railways Habibur Rashid, Road Transport and Highways Division Secretary Dr Mohammed Ziaul Haque, World Bank Division Director for Bangladesh and Bhutan Jean Pesme, representatives of the World Bank and senior officials concerned attended the meeting.

item.title: Adviser: Govt discussing Hasina’s return with India, not with her
item.description:
Prime Minister’s Information and Broadcasting Adviser Zahed Ur Rahman on Tuesday said the government had no communication with former prime minister Sheikh Hasina over her return and was holding discussions with India on the issue.
The adviser made the remarks while responding to a question at a briefing at the Secretariat about a Reuters report quoting Hasina's spokesperson that she intended to return to Bangladesh by a Biman Bangladesh Airlines flight on December 16.
Describing Hasina as a convicted criminal, he said the judicial process against her had been completed and she had been found guilty and sentenced, rather than merely facing allegations.
There should be no legal obstacle to the extradition of Sheikh Hasina if she wants to return to Bangladesh, Zahed Ur Rahman said.
“Bangladesh wants her back and Hasina herself wants to return, so India could extradite her as the positions of both sides are now aligned,” said
The adviser said India had previously cited legal issues regarding her extradition, but he did not see any such obstacle now if Hasina herself wanted to return.
“If Sheikh Hasina wants to come to Bangladesh, I don't think there is any reason for her to go to court or face any legal complications. Her lawyers might try various things if she does not want to come. But if she wants to return, India can simply extradite her and let her come. I don't see any problem now,” he said.
Asked about allegations among Awami League leaders and activists that the government might prevent Hasina from returning at the last moment, Zahed said Hasina herself could request India to extradite her if she believed the government did not want her back.
Such a move, he said, would also make the government's position clear.
He also said Hasina's stated intention to return on December 16 might be an attempt to demonstrate the significance of her decision to her political followers.
“It's a bluff to the political people,” he said.
Explaining the agreement between Bangladesh and India, Zahed said the two countries had an extradition treaty, not a prisoner exchange agreement.
He said prisoner exchange generally implied that one country would hand over a prisoner in return for another, whereas extradition did not involve any such exchange.
Asked about arguments that Hasina had not been taken to India by the Indian authorities but had instead been left there by the then Bangladesh government, the adviser said Bangladesh was effectively without a government at the time.
He said there was no government in place until the interim government, led by Dr Muhammad Yunus, took the oath.
Therefore, he said, it would not be appropriate to use that argument to shift responsibility onto the current elected government.

item.title: 174 undocumented Bangladeshis return from Libya
item.description:
A total of 174 undocumented Bangladeshis who were stranded in Libya and wished to return home voluntarily have been repatriated.
They arrived in Dhaka at 4:45am on Tuesday aboard Buraq Air flight UZ-222.
According to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the repatriation was carried out with the joint cooperation of the Bangladesh Embassy in Libya, the Ministry of Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment, the Libyan government and the International Organization for Migration (IOM).
Most of the returnees had entered Libya illegally after being lured and assisted by human traffickers, hoping to reach Europe by sea, the ministry said. Many reportedly faced abduction and torture in Libya.
Officials from the foreign ministry, other relevant ministries and IOM welcomed them at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport in Dhaka.
The foreign ministry urged the returnees to share their harrowing experiences to raise public awareness about the risks of irregular migration.
IOM provided each returnee with travel expenses, food supplies and basic medical care, as well as temporary accommodation where necessary.
The ministry also said it was working with the Bangladesh Embassy in Libya, the Ministry of Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment and IOM to safely repatriate other Bangladeshis held at detention centres across Libya.

item.title: Nepal’s new PM eyes closer ties with India amid lingering disputes
item.description:
For years, Nepal’s relationship with India was shaped by familiar faces, as leaders of the Himalayan country’s erstwhile three major parties took turns in the prime minister’s office through revolving coalition governments.
This week’s state visit to India by Balendra Shah, a 36-year-old rapper-turned-politician, marked a clear break from that pattern.
As a young, first-time prime minister with a strong electoral mandate, Shah represents a new political force in Kathmandu.
But long-standing economic strain, along with August’s devastating flash floods and the Nepalese public’s high hopes for more jobs, investment and better governance at home, have made Shah’s first bilateral visit abroad more than a mere diplomatic box-ticking exercise.
To safeguard Nepal’s flood recovery and development, Shah needs to get off on the right foot with India, his country’s southern neighbor and largest trading partner, and its long-standing prime minister, Narendra Modi.
While Nepal and India share an open border as well as deep cultural and historical ties, their relationship has also been marked by territorial disputes and a desire in Nepal to be seen as an equal by its much larger and more powerful neighbor.
Constantino Xavier, a senior fellow at the Center for Social and Economic Progress in New Delhi, however, cautioned against expecting too much from a single visit.
“We need a big, long-term ambition coupled with small, short-term steps,” he told DW, arguing that economic cooperation should remain the central focus of relations because it directly contributes to the socioeconomic development of both countries.
The young prime minister’s test is to turn a strong domestic electoral mandate and political goodwill with New Delhi into tangible economic gain, as well as to address longstanding border disputes and a massive trade imbalance.
Shah’s administration sees diplomacy as key to addressing the country’s development aspirations, which was reflected in bilateral talks with Modi on Monday.
Economic cooperation featured prominently during the talks as both sides sought engagements in trade, investment, connectivity and infrastructure development.
Kathmandu’s priority was securing Indian financial support for reconstruction following the August disaster that claimed the lives of more than 1,450 people, while 5,745 are missing or unaccounted for.
The floods swept away roads, bridges, hydropower projects and settlements, with reconstruction bills estimated at around $4.8 billion.
At a joint press briefing after their talks in New Delhi, Modi announced a package of $1.63 billion to help rebuild flood-hit areas and upgrade other infrastructure projects — around $380 million as a grant, with the rest as a concessional loan.
The South Asian neighbors also agreed to deepen cooperation across a wide range of areas, including trade, investment, connectivity and people-to-people ties, and launched a new long-term vision aimed at strengthening economic integration and development.
The talks also yielded commitments to broaden educational and innovation partnerships, boost energy and infrastructure cooperation, improve market access and trade links, and enhance landlocked Nepal’s connectivity through additional air and port access via India.
Shah’s visit offered an opportunity to break the ice in a high-level exchange visit and improve a relationship periodically strained by political mistrust, territorial disputes and differing strategic interests.
Nepal and India both have competing territorial claims over Kalapani, Lipulekh and Limpiyadhura, a strategic Himalayan territory in northwestern Nepal.
As mayor of Kathmandu, Shah raised the border disputes with India, which helped boost his nationalist image and set his broader political agenda. However, his India visit steered clear of such contentious issues.
Bimala Rai Paudyal, a former Foreign Minister of Nepal, said Shah avoided tricky bilateral issues to focus on his administration’s economic agenda.
“This visit could be a good starting point towards resolving the border issues that have been the key strain in our relations,” she told DW. “But the new government didn’t show interest or the guts to address this.”
Ashok Swain, head of the Department of Peace and Conflict Research at Sweden’s Uppsala University, said the visit’s success should be measured by whether the two countries can establish a predictable and mutually beneficial relationship.
“Nepal’s territorial disputes, concerns over the 1950 Treaty of Peace and Friendship and its economic and transit dependence on India need to be addressed,” Swain told DW.
“Shah’s biggest opportunity is to transform Nepal’s geographical location between India and China from a strategic vulnerability into an economic and diplomatic asset,” he added, arguing that Nepal should not be forced to choose between its two neighbors.
Whether the visit marks a tangible reset on the economic front will ultimately depend not on the number of agreements announced, but on how they are implemented and whether the two governments are willing to address the disputes that have long strained ties.

item.title: 14 countries ‘acknowledge’ ICJ ruling on Rohingya ‘genocide’
item.description:
The UK and 13 other countries on Monday “acknowledged” the top UN court’s ruling that Myanmar perpetrated genocide against its Rohingya minority as London announced new sanctions.
The foreign ministers of Australia, Belgium, Canada, Cyprus, Czech Republic, Estonia, Iceland, Latvia, Luxembourg, New Zealand, Portugal, Spain, The Gambia and the United Kingdom said Myanmar had “violated its obligations under the Genocide Convention.”
“We underscore that the Court’s judgment is binding upon Myanmar and call on Myanmar to comply fully with its obligations under international law, including the Court’s decision,” they said in a joint statement.
The UK separately said it “formally recognizes” genocide against the Rohingya and announced sanctions on five senior military figures.
“The horrific violence and persecution inflicted on the Rohingya cannot go unanswered,” UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband said.
The sanctions include asset freezes and travel bans, a Foreign Office statement said, adding that London “also intends to introduce legislation targeting the export and supply of aviation fuel to Myanmar.”
“The UK is providing an additional £5m in new funding to support Rohingya and other communities with essential lifesaving and life-affirming services to approximately 350,000 people who need it most in Rakhine state, where humanitarian need is most acute,” the statement added.
It said a further £3 million would “go towards strengthening accountability and justice for survivors of human rights abuses across Myanmar.”
On November 19 in a historic verdict, the International Court of Justice (ICJ) ruled Myanmar committed genocide against its Rohingya minority during a 2017 crackdown in the western Rakhine state.
The ruling was the first time in the ICJ’s 80-year history that it has determined that a state committed genocide.
Myanmar’s government called the ruling unfair and a “great disappointment.”
Shortly after the verdict, Britain announced it would expel Myanmar’s defense attaché.

item.title: Govt to award laptops to 1,500 top SSC achievers
item.description:
The government has taken an initiative to award laptops to 1,500 meritorious students who secured GPA-5 in all subjects in this year's Secondary School Certificate (SSC) and equivalent examinations.
The initiative was taken by the Secondary and Higher Education Division of the Ministry of Education at the directive of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman to recognize their academic excellence and encouraging greater engagement with modern technology.
Under the initiative, the top 100 highest-scoring students from each of the country's 11 education boards will be selected on the basis of merit, taking the total number of initial recipients to 1,100.
An additional 400 laptops will be kept in reserve to accommodate the candidates securing equal marks at the 100th position.
The programme will be implemented under the scheme titled "Strengthening Reading Habit among Secondary Students", under the Secondary Education Development Programme (SEDP) aimed at promoting academic excellence and equipping students with modern technological skills.
The government plans to procure the laptops in accordance with the Public Procurement Rules (PPR)-2025 and distribute them among the selected students by February-March 2027.
Education and Primary and Mass Education Minister Dr ANM Ehsanul Hoque Milon told BSS that the government had decided to initially award laptops to the top 1,500 students selected on merit from the 11 education boards.
"We have decided to provide laptops to the top 1,500 students from the 11 education boards in the initial phase. The programme will be expanded further through various initiatives," he said.
He added that 400 additional laptops had been reserved to address cases where multiple students secured identical marks at the 100th position.
The government is also considering introducing similar incentives for meritorious students at the HSC level.
According to Education Ministry officials, the initial plan was to provide laptops to 40,000 students who secured GPA-5 in all subjects. However, the government has opted for a phased implementation, beginning with 1,500 recipients.
The estimated expenditure for the first phase is Tk16-17 crore.
Professor Md Firoz Alam, director of the scheme, told BSS that the initiative was designed not only to recognise academic achievement but also to familiarise students with artificial intelligence (AI) and modern information technology.
He said the education boards would verify their respective databases and submit the final selection lists to ensure a transparent, merit-based process.
Alam also emphasised that the laptops would have modern features and quality configurations. A formal distribution programme involving all 11 education boards is being planned.
The selection will be determined by students' total marks rather than GPA-5 alone, following the framework developed by the Dhaka Education Board.
Under the distribution formula, 50% of the selected students will come from the science group, 30% from the humanities group and 20% from the business studies group, taking into account the number and proportion of examinees in each group.
Officials said the same formula had been followed by the other eight general education boards, while the Technical Education Board and Madrasa Education Board adopted slightly different selection procedures to reflect their respective academic structures.
Professor Syed Akhtaruzzaman, President of the Inter-Education Board Coordination Committee and Chairman of the Dhaka Education Board, told BSS that the top 100 highest-scoring students from each board had been selected in accordance with the ministry's instructions.
The final lists from all 11 boards had already been submitted to the ministry.
Engr Md Abul Kalam Azad said the lists of top GPA-5 achievers in the SSC Vocational and Dakhil Vocational examinations had been prepared and forwarded to the coordination committee.
He explained that students from the two streams had been selected proportionately, considering the significantly lower number of candidates in Dakhil Vocational compared to SSC Vocational.
Madrasah Education Board Controller of Examinations Professor Md Faruk Ahmed said the board had prepared and submitted a list of the highest-scoring students who secured GPA-5 in all subjects in the Dakhil examination.
He said the selection also considered the proportional representation of students from the science, humanities and Mujabbid groups.
Meanwhile, Director General of the Directorate of Secondary and Higher Education Bangladesh, Dhaka Prof. Dr. Khan Moinuddin Al Mahmud Sohel told BSS that the Ministry of Finance had given its consent to the distribution of laptops among the 1,500 students.
He said the initiative reflected the government's commitment to motivating students to excel academically while enabling them to develop technological competencies essential for higher education and future professional pursuits.
This year, the average pass rate in the SSC and equivalent examinations across the 11 education boards stood at 62.25%, while 116,676 students achieved GPA-5.

item.title: Canada vows faster visas, more jobs for skilled Bangladeshis
item.description:
Canada has pledged to expedite and simplify visa processing for Bangladeshi travellers, students and businesspeople, while expressing interest in recruiting skilled workers from Bangladesh and expanding cooperation in cybersecurity.
The assurances came from Weldon Epp, assistant deputy minister for the Indo-Pacific at Global Affairs Canada, during a courtesy call on Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed at the Secretariat on Tuesday.
Foysal Hasan, deputy chief information officer of the Home Ministry, said the meeting discussed issues of mutual interest, including curbing irregular migration, exporting skilled manpower, cybersecurity, joint investment and resolving the Rohingya crisis.
At the outset, the home minister described Bangladesh and Canada as longstanding friends and development partners.
In response, Epp said that despite efforts to balance its immigration policy, Canada remained interested in welcoming talented Bangladeshi students and skilled professionals.
He assured the minister that visa processing for legitimate travellers, students and businesspeople from Bangladesh would be made faster and easier.
Salahuddin Ahmed urged Canada to recruit skilled workers from Bangladesh through legal channels in line with its labour market needs.
He said Bangladesh had a large pool of trained professionals in nursing, medical technology, home care, marine services and hospitality. Canada could help develop the required workforce by sending trainers to Bangladesh or establishing specialised training academies through joint initiatives.
Welcoming the proposal, Epp said Canada's economy had a growing demand for skilled workers, particularly nurses and caregivers.
The two sides also discussed expanding bilateral trade and investment. The home minister expressed Bangladesh's interest in acquiring advanced technology, including river and coastal patrol vessels for the Coast Guard and cybersecurity and communication equipment for the police.
On the Rohingya crisis, Epp said Canada had increased the number of Rohingya refugees it resettled from Bangladesh despite its efforts to limit overall immigration.
He said Canada was also working to encourage greater involvement by regional countries, particularly members of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN), in resolving the crisis.
Highlighting Bangladesh's generosity in sheltering a large Rohingya population, Salahuddin said China, ASEAN and the international community should increase pressure on Myanmar following the International Court of Justice (ICJ) ruling.
He stressed the need to ensure citizenship, access to safe land and livelihood opportunities so that the Rohingya could return to their homeland voluntarily.
The minister also described cyber fraud, drug trafficking and human trafficking originating from Myanmar as serious regional and global security threats, calling for coordinated efforts to combat the crimes.
Canadian High Commissioner to Bangladesh Ajit Singh, Home Ministry Additional Secretary (Political and Immigration) Dr Ziauddin Ahmed, Joint Secretary of the Political-1 Wing Rebecca Khan, Canadian High Commission Political Counsellor Marcus Davis, Head of Aid Suzanne Quinn, Trade Commissioner Kamal Uddin and senior officials from both sides attended the meeting.

item.title: 887 women killed over dowry in 5 years
item.description:
“My daughter was crying. She was calling me on a video call, saying, ‘Father, come and save me.’ Imagine how I felt as a father!”

Sheikh Manowar Hossain could not reach his daughter, Jumratun Nesa Barsha, alive that day.

Speaking to Prothom Alo on 14 November, his voice was filled with grief and regret. He said, “I was bare-chested. I kept my daughter on the video call and rushed downstairs with a shirt in one hand, telling her, ‘I’m coming, dear, I’m coming.’ It was 12:15 am! It takes us 15 to 20 minutes by rickshaw to reach her in-laws’ home in Monipuripara. When we got there, my daughter was gone!”

Barsha was taken to Shaheed Suhrawardy Medical College Hospital in the capital in an unconscious state on the night of 28 October. Physicians declared her dead. After a call was made to the national emergency service 999, police from Tejgaon Police Station arrived.

Barsha's family handed her husband, Nabid Hossain, over to the police. A case was filed at Tejgaon Police Station under Section 11(a) of the Women and Children Repression Prevention Act, accusing her husband of causing her death over dowry. Her father is the complainant.

According to Police Headquarters data, 887 cases have been filed over the past five years on allegations of murder over dowry. Of these, 487 were filed with police stations, while the rest were filed in court.

Prothom Alo spoke to the families of three women who died in incidents linked to dowry. Some parents said, “Our daughter was very dear to us.” Others said, “We never even hit our daughter.” Their anguish was summed up in one desperate plea: “Our daughter is gone! We are finished too! Please help us get justice!”

Amid such appeals from parents seeking justice, the 16 Days of Activism against Gender-Based Violence begins today, Wednesday. Observed worldwide from 25 November to 10 December every year, the campaign calls for an end to violence against women.

Cases of murder, suicide and abuse linked to dowry expose the devastating scale of this long-standing social crime.

According to Ain o Salish Kendra (ASK), a non-governmental organisation, 472 reports of dowry-related abuse were published in the media over four years and 10 months, from 2022 to October 2026.

Of these, 220 women were killed as a result of dowry-related abuse. Another 21 women died by suicide after being unable to endure such abuse. A total of 301 cases were filed in connection with the 472 incidents.

Under the Dowry Prohibition Act 2018, if either party to a marriage demands dowry, directly or indirectly, from the other party, it constitutes an offence. The punishment is imprisonment for a minimum of one year and a maximum of five years, a fine of up to Tk 50,000, or both.

Under Section 11 of the Women and Children Repression Prevention Act 2000, causing death over dowry is a punishable offence. Depending on the severity of the offence, the law provides for rigorous imprisonment of at least two years and up to the death penalty.

Of the cases filed over alleged dowry-related murders in the past five years, nearly half were filed in court rather than at police stations.
Asked why, Assistant Inspector General (Media and Public Relations) of Police Headquarters Kamarum Munira told Prothom Alo that attempts were often made to settle dowry-related incidents through various means. Families came under pressure and delayed filing cases at police stations. As a result, they eventually approached the courts to file cases.

Abuse continued for a long time

Barsha was the second of three daughters of Sheikh Manowar Hossain and Hasina Akter, permanent residents of Lalbagh in the capital. She was a first-year honours student at Tejgaon College. Barsha and Nabid Hossain had their marriage contract solemnised on 7 October last year. The formal wedding ceremony was scheduled for January next year.

Barsha's father, Manowar Hossain, is involved in the land trading business. He told Prothom Alo that Nabid had once beaten Barsha so severely, six to seven months earlier, that her head was injured. The family had taken her to hospital at the time and wanted to file a case, but they could not do so because Barsha objected.

Manowar Hossain alleged that Nabid had taken money from him several times on the pretext of running a business.

Overcome with emotion while talking about his daughter, he said, “My daughter was very dear to me. I gave her whatever she wanted. I never said no to her. There must be justice for my daughter's murder.”

The body of Sumaiya Akter, 16, was recovered from her in-laws' home in Salampur village of Shahbajpur union in Shibganj upazila of Chapainawabganj on 28 April. Sumaiya's parents live in Pirojpur village in the same union. Her husband had taken her from her parents' home, and the following day the family received news that she was ill. When her parents rushed to her in-laws' home, they found that she had died.

Sumaiya's mother, Runa Begum, filed a case at Shibganj Police Station under Section 11(a) of the Women and Children Repression Prevention Act, accusing her daughter''s husband of killing her over dowry.

Speaking to Prothom Alo on 16 November, she said her son-in-law had repeatedly pressured Sumaiya to bring money to buy a battery-powered autorickshaw. He had also threatened not to continue the marriage if the money was not provided.

Runa Begum said Sumaiya survived for only five months after her marriage. She would frequently return to her parents' home after being beaten.

She said, “How many times Sumaiya's grandmother called her husband's father and told him, ‘We have never beaten our daughter. Please don't beat her. We cannot give you all the money to buy the vehicle (autorickshaw) at once. We will pay it gradually.’”

Sub-Inspector (SI) Md Bedar Uddin, the investigation officer of the case, told Prothom Alo that a recent post-mortem report had described the incident as a suicide. He said further investigation would be necessary.
Sumaiya's husband, who was under 18 at the time, is being held at the Jashore Child Development Centre in connection with the case. Her father-in-law, Mahabubur Rahman, is in the district jail following his arrest.

‘I have been to court 70–80 times in nine years, but there has been no verdict’

Seema Rani died on 16 June 2017, four years after her marriage, at Doleswar in Keraniganj. Her only son was eight months old at the time. Her body bore marks of injuries and burns.

The case filed over her alleged dowry-related murder is still at the witness examination stage at the Dhaka Women and Children Repression Prevention Tribunal-4. Bangladesh Legal Aid and Services Trust (BLAST) is providing legal assistance to the complainant's side.

Seema's father, Dulal Chandra Mali, an occasional performer at Bangladesh Betar, told Prothom Alo on 17 November that their home was beside Barishal Medical College. Seema was the younger of his two children. Her son now lives with his maternal grandparents.

Seema's husband, Gopal Chandra Mali, and the other accused were released on bail after serving just nine months in jail. Gopal remarried after securing bail.

Dulal Chandra Mali said, “I have travelled to Dhaka to attend court hearings 70 to 80 times so far, but there has been no verdict. For the past one and a half to two years, the accused have kept the case pending by failing to produce witnesses.”

Expressing his frustration, he said, “My daughter is gone! We are finished too! Please help us get justice!”

Seema's father said he had given Tk 300,000 to her husband at the time of their marriage. Despite this, her husband continued to torture her, demanding more dowry to run his salon business.

‘The government must take a firm stand’

In 2020, Professor Muhammad Umar Faruk, chairman of the Department of Criminology and Police Science at Mawlana Bhashani Science and Technology University, conducted a study on domestic violence involving 390 women across eight divisions.

The study found that 87 per cent of women in the country had experienced one or more forms of domestic violence—physical, psychological, economic or sexual. Only 1 per cent of the victims filed cases, while nearly 3 per cent sought mediation through arbitration or non-governmental organisations (NGOs).

Fawzia Moslem, president of the Bangladesh Mahila Parishad, told Prothom Alo that dowry-related killings of women had reached an alarming level. She said dowry was being extracted in various ways.
She also pointed to the emergence of a form of misogynistic subculture.

A particular group, she said, was spreading misinformation by claiming that 90 per cent of dowry-related cases were false, thereby encouraging the practice of demanding dowry.

Fawzia Moslem further said a social movement was needed to raise awareness against dowry. The government must take a firm stand as part of its political responsibility, she said, so that delays in dowry-related cases could be reduced and those seeking justice could regain confidence in the judicial process.

item.description:
The government is not under any pressure over ousted former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina's announcement to return to Bangladesh on 16 December, said Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed.

He noted that the heightened alert of law enforcement agencies across the country is part of the government's regular duties.

“She keeps saying she will return. At one point, she said she would come in November, then she said December. We don't know when she will return. The government is not focused on this, nor is it under any pressure,” Salahuddin Ahmed said.

The home minister said Hasina could be extradited under the extradition treaty. A letter has been sent to India through diplomatic channels and India has said it is examining the matter in accordance with the law and taking steps accordingly.

He made the remarks at a press conference in the meeting room of the Ministry of Home Affairs at the Secretariat on Wednesday.

Salahuddin Ahmed said some police and other law enforcement officials are still affiliated with fascist forces and are involved in conspiracies. They are under strict government surveillance. Action is being taken against some of them, he said.

Regarding the investigation into crimes against humanity involving Awami League, whose activities are now banned, as a party, the home minister said action will be taken in accordance with the court's verdict after the investigation, charge sheet and judicial proceedings are completed. The Election Commission will take the necessary steps, he added.

On garment workers' wages, Salahuddin Ahmed said those taking to the streets to protest even after wages have been determined are not workers. They do not have the support of workers either. The authorities will investigate who is behind the protests, he said.

The home minister said fascist forces are calling lockdowns and shutdowns but the people of Bangladesh would not allow them to succeed. BGB is being deployed in various districts, he said, adding that law enforcement agencies are showing considerable restraint.

The government has tactfully ensured that there are no civilian casualties, and will continue to do so in the future. However, if anyone engages in destructive activities, they will be strictly contained.

Salahuddin Ahmed also said that forces ousted for committing genocide have never been able to return to politics or regain power. They will never be able to engage in politics again, he said.

He added that the situation in Gopalganj had been handled without any loss of life. Anyone seeking to engage in extremist or destructive activities will face strict action.

item.title: China space station receives Pakistani astronaut on 'historic mission'
item.description:
CORRECTION-TOPSHOT-CHINA-SPACE-SHENZHOU-PAKISTAN

China's space station welcomed its first foreign lodger on Wednesday as a Pakistani astronaut boarded the Tiangong with his Shenzhou-24 mission crew, Beijing said.

China has poured billions into its space programme as it aims to land astronauts on the Moon before 2030, a race in which the United States is also competing with its Artemis programme.

The Shenzhou-24 crew's Long March 2-F rocket took off in a cloud of flames and smoke Wednesday morning from the Jiuquan launch centre in northwestern China under a pink sky, video from state broadcaster CCTV showed.

The spacecraft successfully separated from the carrier rocket roughly 10 minutes after blast-off and entered into orbit, the China Manned Space Agency (CMSA) said.

The launch was a "complete success" and the crew was in good condition, the agency said.

After roughly three-and-a-half hours from launch, the Shenzhou-24 spacecraft successfully docked at the Tiangong space station, according to CMSA.

Along with Pakistani astronaut Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, the latest mission is crewed by Chinese spacecraft pilot Tang Hongbo and Chinese flight engineer Wu Yi.

The three men "successfully moved into" the Tiangong, completing the first "space handshake" between Chinese and foreign astronauts, CMSA said in a statement.

Pakistan and China are close diplomatic and strategic partners, and signed a deal in February 2025 setting up a Chinese government training programme for Pakistani astronauts.

Chinese President Xi Jinping exchanged congratulations with his Pakistani counterpart after the launch, telling Asif Ali Zardari that Beijing stood ready to champion the "peaceful use of outer space" and "improve global space governance", according to CCTV.

On Monday, NATO chief Mark Rutte said the alliance would defend against threats in space, after reports said Russia may be preparing to launch a nuclear-armed satellite.

'Historic mission'

Now aboard the Tiangong station, Ali, a Pakistan Air Force pilot and payload specialist, is the first foreign astronaut to fly on a Chinese space mission.

Pakistan's space agency said he would conduct experiments in orbit, including cultivating microalgae as a potential food and oxygen source for future space missions, and testing the effects of spaceflight on quinoa seeds.

The 40-year-old will join a short orbital flight expected to last around five days before returning with the Shenzhou-23 spaceship, which docked at the Tiangong space station in May.

That ship's crew includes astronauts Zhu Yangzhu, Lai Ka-ying and Zhang Zhiyuan.

Lai is Hong Kong's first astronaut and the only woman currently aboard.

Ali is not the first Pakistani in space, with Monaco-based polar adventurer Namira Salim having flown on Virgin Galactic's Galactic 04 mission in October 2023.

Still, Pakistan's Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar on Wednesday called the Shenzhou-24 launch a "historic mission", marking a milestone in his country's partnership with China.

"A proud moment for Pakistan, this mission will inspire our youth and advance our aspirations in science and technology," he wrote on social media.

Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif previously hailed the mission as a testament to their close ties.

"Pakistan-China friendship is surpassing the heights of the Himalayas, in its journey to outer space," he said.

Ali is scheduled to return to Earth alongside Lai and Zhang.

Zhu will remain on board to complete China's first full-year stay in space -- a key test of endurance critical for future lunar and potentially deep-space ambitions.

item.title: 10 development projects involving Tk24,110cr get ECNEC nod
item.description:
The Executive Committee of the National Economic Council (ECNEC) on Wednesday approved 10 projects involving Tk24,110.66 crore.
Of the total, Tk 12,775.99 crore will come from the government's own funds, Tk 8,944.21 crore from project loans and Tk 2,390.47 crore from the agencies' own resources.
Prime Minister and ECNEC Chairperson Tarique Rahman presided over the meeting at the secretariat.
Of the 10 projects, five are new, four are revised and one has been granted a time extension.
The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare secured approval for two projects.
One is the second revision of the project to set up full-fledged cancer, heart and kidney treatment centres in eight divisional cities.
The other is the second revision of the project to build 500-bed medical college hospitals and ancillary buildings in Jessore, Cox's Bazar, Pabna and Noakhali, along with the vertical extension of the National Institute of Gastroliver Diseases and Hospital by adding 11th and 12th floors.
The Ministry of Social Welfare received approval for a fourth time extension of the project to set up a Bangladesh Poverty Alleviation Organisation health service centre in Charfesson Upazila.
Three projects of the Ministry of Local Government, Rural Development and Cooperatives were approved.

item.title: NBR cuts import duties on dates, apples, and oranges ahead of Ramadan
item.description:
The National Board of Revenue (NBR) has reduced import duties on dates, apples, and oranges to keep their prices under control during the upcoming holy month of Ramadan.
According to a gazette notification issued on Tuesday, the import duty on dates has been slashed from 25% to 5%, bringing the total tax incidence on date imports down from 48% to 25%.
This reduced rate will remain in effect until March 10, 2027.
For apples and oranges, the regulatory duty has been reduced to 5%, while supplementary duty and VAT have been set at 20%.
Following these adjustments, the total tax incidence on apples and oranges will drop sharply from 121% to 48%.
The notification stated that the revised rates for apples and oranges will be effective from January 24 to February 23, 2027.
The NBR expects that the duty cuts will boost imports and ensure an adequate supply of these fruits, helping to stabilize market prices.
The decision to lower duties on these import-dependent fruits was reportedly taken a few days ago during a cabinet meeting chaired by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman.
Currently, different varieties of dates are selling between Tk200 and Tk2,000 per kilogram in Dhaka’s kitchen markets, while apples are priced at Tk300–500 per kg and oranges at Tk400–600 per kg.

item.title: Bangladesh among 14 economies facing fresh US tariffs
item.description:
Bangladesh is among 14 major US trading partners facing fresh tariffs proposed by the administration of President Donald Trump on Wednesday, following a months-long investigation into alleged excess manufacturing capacity and production.
The proposed duties, reaching up to 20% under the rates outlined by a senior US official, mark another escalation in Washington’s efforts to reshape global trade and could create fresh uncertainty for Bangladesh’s export-oriented industries, particularly the ready-made garment sector.
The specific tariff rate applicable to Bangladesh was not immediately clear.
The proposed duties will undergo a public consultation process before taking effect, potentially as early as January 2027.
However, a senior US official said the proposals would take existing trade agreements into account, offering some relief to countries that have already negotiated tariff arrangements with Washington.
The official also said the new duties would not be imposed on top of tariffs introduced in July over alleged failures to address forced labour.
For economies subject to both measures, the higher of the two rates would apply.
Bangladesh was among the countries subjected to a 10% tariff under the July measures, with certain product exemptions.
Besides Bangladesh, the proposed tariffs target China, the European Union, India, Cambodia, Indonesia, Japan, South Korea, Malaysia, Singapore, Switzerland, Taiwan, Thailand and Vietnam.
The measures also cover several of Bangladesh’s major competitors in the global garment market, including China, Vietnam, India, Cambodia and Indonesia.
The senior US official, speaking on condition of anonymity, alleged that the targeted economies were promoting production and industrial capacity that did not reflect actual market demand.
Washington has proposed a 20% tariff on China, one of the highest rates under the latest measures.
In a separate announcement, the Office of the United States Trade Representative (USTR) proposed additional tariffs on Brazilian goods, including aircraft, citing alleged failures to address US trade concerns.
The latest tariff proposals follow an investigation launched by the USTR in March into alleged excess manufacturing capacity and production among major US trading partners.
The investigation examined whether foreign industrial policies and practices were unreasonable or discriminatory and whether they adversely affected US commerce.
The probe was launched shortly after the US Supreme Court struck down Trump’s previous sweeping global tariffs, ruling that the president lacked the authority to impose them under the law cited by the White House.
Trade lawyer Ryan Majerus told AFP that the investigation could become one of the Trump administration’s most consequential trade actions.
He explained that Washington was concerned about factories overseas continuing production despite insufficient demand, potentially creating an oversupply of goods, depressing prices and undermining US manufacturing.
The US determination is likely to face resistance from China and other affected economies. Beijing has long rejected accusations that its economic growth relies excessively on exports.
The latest proposals come as Trump prepares to host G20 leaders in Miami in December.
Despite the potential for renewed trade tensions, the senior US official expressed optimism that the measures could lead to further trade negotiations.
“We don’t expect this to create tension or rancor” at the G20 summit, the official said, adding that Washington anticipated signing more agreements following the announcements.
The official said concerns over excess industrial capacity extended across several sectors, including batteries, cement, chemicals and processed food.
The proposed duties will not be imposed cumulatively with existing sector-specific tariffs on products such as automobiles and steel.
Those sector-specific measures remain in force despite the Supreme Court’s February ruling against Trump’s broader global tariffs.
For Bangladesh, the immediate concern is the final tariff rate, the scope of product exemptions and how the proposed measures will affect its export competitiveness relative to other garment-producing economies.
The full implications will become clearer once Washington finalises the country-specific tariff schedules following the public consultation process.

item.title: Gopalganj violence: Probe turns to police, administration, money trail; 101 accounts frozen
item.description:
Intelligence agencies investigating the recent sabotage and violence in Gopalganj have turned their attention to police and administrative officials, alongside political leaders. They are looking beyond those who carried out the mayhem on the ground, to who provided the money, who incited the violence and who assisted it from within the administration.
A company commander of the Special Response Battalion (SRB), a specialised police unit, has been arrested. At the same time, the National Board of Revenue (NBR) has frozen the bank accounts of 97 individuals and four business establishments over allegations of financing and supporting the violence. They include a former secretary, leaders at various levels of the activities banned Awami League, and public representatives.
The activities of law enforcement agencies and revenue intelligence have brought to light another alarming aspect of the conspiracy behind the violence. Investigators are seeking answers to two questions: whether an organised network was active behind the acts of sabotage carried out under the cover of political programmes, and whether there were internal links within the administration with the political and financial patronage.
Intelligence sources say it is difficult to prevent a recurrence of sabotage by arresting only those who carried out attacks at the field level. For this reason, initiatives have been taken to identify and bring to justice the possible organisers, financiers and associates behind the violence. The freezing of bank accounts and the surveillance of police and administrative officials are part of this investigation.
Questions have been raised about the role of law enforcement agencies in the widespread sabotage and violence in Gopalganj surrounding recent programmes of the activities banned Awami League.
Intelligence agencies are investigating whether anyone within the police and administration had contact with, or links of assistance with, those involved in the sabotage following the arson at Muksudpur police station.
At least more than three dozen police and administrative officials in the greater Faridpur region have been placed under intelligence surveillance in connection with the sabotage. Agencies are examining whether they had any direct or indirect involvement in the violence.
The investigation is also looking into whether any administrative official used their position, designation and influence to assist the sabotage, or deliberately remained inactive in carrying out their duties and thereby created an opportunity for the violence.
Those concerned do not want to disclose the names and designations of the officials under surveillance, or the information obtained against them, at this stage in the interest of the investigation.
Asked about these matters, Additional Inspector General of Police (Crime and Ops) Ahsan Habib Palash told Dhaka Tribune that he did not know how many people were under surveillance.
Additional Superintendent of Police Md Abul Hasan, who came into discussion following the arson at Muksudpur police station, was arrested on Monday (November 23) night from the SRB-14 office in Mymensingh by a team of the Detective Branch (DB) of Dhaka Metropolitan Police.
According to relevant sources, he was arrested on the basis of intelligence information about his involvement in the recent sabotage in Gopalganj surrounding programmes of the activities banned Awami League.
Before August 5, 2024, Abul Hasan served in various important positions, including in the Counter Terrorism and Transnational Crime (CTTC) unit of Dhaka Metropolitan Police. Later, he was transferred to the SRB. Most recently, he was working as a company commander at SRB-14 in Mymensingh.
However, although sources said he had been arrested over allegations of involvement in the Gopalganj sabotage, he was shown as arrested in court in the case filed over the attack on the BNP central office and the murder of party worker Makbul Hossain.
On Tuesday (November 24) afternoon, Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate of Dhaka Jashita Islam ordered that he be sent to jail after the hearing. Rokonuzzaman, an assistant sub-inspector of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police Prosecution Division, confirmed the information.
Dhaka Metropolitan Police Additional Commissioner (Detective) Md Shafiqul Islam told Dhaka Tribune: "Additional Superintendent of Police Abul Hasan, who was working at the SRB, was not arrested in connection with the incident in Gopalganj. He was arrested as a named accused in a murder case at Paltan police station. The DB is investigating the case."
DB Sub-Inspector Md Toffazzal Hossain, the investigation officer in the case, applied to have Abul Hasan produced before the court and kept in jail.
In the application, he stated that, based on information obtained from various sources during the investigation, preliminary allegations had emerged against Abul Hasan that he had assisted the then government in suppressing its political opponents. During interrogation, he provided some information about the murder. The information will be verified and examined before necessary measures are taken.
The case is currently being investigated by the Motijheel Division of Dhaka Metropolitan Police's Detective Branch. The investigation officer also told the court that, if necessary in the interest of the investigation, an application would later be made to take him into police custody for questioning.
On December 7, 2022, BNP worker Makbul Hossain died after being shot during clashes surrounding the BNP central office in Nayapaltan in the capital. After the fall of the Awami League government, a person named Mahfuzur Rahman filed a case over the incident at Paltan Model Police Station on September 30, 2024. In the case, in which 256 people, including former prime minister Sheikh Hasina, were named as accused, Abul Hasan is accused number 171 in the first information report.
One of the biggest steps in the investigation concerns the financial sector. The NBR has frozen the bank accounts of 97 individuals and four business establishments over allegations of financing the violence and supporting efforts to create instability.
Over the past three days, separate letters have been sent to the relevant banks, instructing them to freeze the accounts of those on the list. Documents relating to their financial transactions are also being collected.
Several officials from banks and the NBR confirmed the matter. They said preliminary investigations had found some information and evidence of irregularities in the financial transactions of those listed. Further investigations are under way to determine whether these transactions are linked to the recent violence in Gopalganj.
The investigation will examine the sources of their money, who transferred money to whose account, what the money was used for, and whether there is any connection between the transactions and the allegations of financing sabotage.
A senior NBR official said a list of those whose bank account transactions had so far been found to contain irregularities had been published. Officials of intelligence agencies are working on the matter. The number may increase further. Some more sensational information will be disclosed very soon, the official said.
A review of the list shows that it includes former bureaucrats, influential leaders at district and upazila levels of the activities banned Awami League, former and current public representatives, and businesspeople. Former Health Secretary Sirajul Haque Khan and his wife Ashrafun Nahar are on the list.
Among the political leaders are Gopalganj district Awami League Vice-President Chowdhury Khasrul Alam, Gopalganj Sadar Upazila Chairman and Awami League leader Kamruzzaman Bhuiyan, and Vice-Chairman Sushil Biswas (Shipon).
The accounts of Babul Sheikh, general secretary of Tungipara Upazila Awami League and former chairman of the upazila parishad, have also been frozen. So have those of Bhabendranath Biswas and Ainal Hossain Sheikh, president and general secretary respectively of Kotalipara Upazila Awami League.
Also on the list are Muksudpur Upazila Awami League President Robiul Alam Sikder, former upazila parishad chairman Kabir Mia, Bhaworshur Union Parishad Chairman SM Rifat ul Alam, and Kashiani Upazila Awami League President and former upazila parishad chairman Moktar Hossain.
However, detailed information is not yet available on what kinds of transactions have been found against each person, how much money they are accused of using for sabotage, or who had financial links with whom.
According to NBR information, the frozen accounts include 32 people from Kotalipara, 19 from Kashiani, 17 from Gopalganj Sadar, 15 from Tungipara and 14 from Muksudpur.
The four commercial establishments whose accounts have been frozen include businesses in the housing and transport sectors. Investigators are examining their business activities, income tax documents and bank account transactions.
This is not the first time bank accounts have been frozen over allegations of financing political instability and violence. Earlier, the NBR had frozen the accounts of 204 individuals, including former ministers, members of parliament, political leaders and leading businesspeople, over allegations of financing and providing manpower to support garment workers' protests. This time, a similar measure has been taken in connection with the sabotage in Gopalganj.
A senior official at Police Headquarters told Dhaka Tribune that efforts were under way to identify the possible networks behind the sabotage through two processes: law enforcement operations and intelligence surveillance at the field level, and restrictions on the financial transactions of suspected financiers.
Those concerned say that although financial transactions can be controlled by freezing bank accounts, proving allegations of financing sabotage requires specific information about the source, destination and use of the money. Finding irregular transactions in a bank account and finding evidence of financing sabotage are not the same thing. Further legal action against these individuals and organisations will therefore depend on more detailed investigation.
Dr Md Tawohidul Haque, an associate professor at the Institute of Social Welfare and Research of Dhaka University and a crime analyst, told Dhaka Tribune:
"Alongside identifying the financiers and political organisers behind the sabotage in Gopalganj, special importance must be given to investigating possible associates within the police and administration. This is because if anyone among the officials responsible for maintaining law and order is involved, in addition to the involvement of field-level activists in political violence, the matter is not limited to a criminal offence alone. It also raises questions about the professionalism and discipline of the force, administrative neutrality and the credibility of the state's security system."

item.title: Indian minister’s callous rhetoric: ‘Taking over Bangladesh’ by December 16
item.description:
Apparently, running Indian state of West Bengal’s transport affairs is no longer ambitious enough for its transport minister, Arjun Singh.
He has now set his sights on an entire sovereign country, Bangladesh, and even announced a deadline for its takeover: December 16.
In a remarkable display of political bravado, the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) minister threatened on Tuesday to take over Bangladesh, invoking alleged killings of Hindus as justification for his territorial ambitions.
“By December 16, we will take over Bangladesh. The way Hindus have been killed in Bangladesh, we will definitely avenge that; there is no doubt about it,” Singh told reporters in Bhatpara, West Bengal, according to Indian media reports.
The irony of his chosen deadline appears to have escaped the minister.
December 16 is Bangladesh’s Victory Day, commemorating the surrender of Pakistani occupation forces in 1971 after a nine-month Liberation War, a war in which India itself played a crucial role in securing Bangladesh’s independence.
More than half a century later, an Indian state minister is invoking that very date to threaten the sovereignty of the nation India once helped liberate.
Singh offered no explanation of how he intended to accomplish his extraordinary territorial ambition within three weeks.
Nor did he explain under what authority a state-level transport minister could announce the takeover of an internationally recognised sovereign nation.
India’s defence, security and foreign affairs fall under the jurisdiction of its central government, not the transport department of West Bengal.
There is no indication that Singh’s remarks reflect any official policy or decision by New Delhi.
Nevertheless, the comments go beyond ordinary political rhetoric, raising questions about the growing recklessness of political discourse surrounding Bangladesh in sections of Indian politics.
Interestingly, Singh’s territorial ambitions coincide with another announcement concerning Bangladesh’s Victory Day.
Former prime minister Sheikh Hasina, who has been living in India for more than two years since her departure on August 5, 2024, has expressed her intention to return to Bangladesh on December 16.
Her spokesperson, Syed Mozammel Ali, said in a statement on Tuesday that Hasina had requested the Bangladesh government to arrange her return from New Delhi aboard a Biman Bangladesh Airlines flight.
She had also sought the necessary travel documents from the Bangladesh High Commission in New Delhi through communications sent by her lawyer on November 9 and 19.

item.title: Jaiswal: India examining Hasina extradition request under established procedure
item.description:
India’s Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal has said that the extradition request for former prime minister Sheikh Hasina, who was sentenced to death for crimes against humanity and is currently in India, is being examined according to established procedures.
He made the statement during the Indian Ministry of External Affairs’ weekly briefing on Wednesday.
Asked about Sheikh Hasina’s possible return to Bangladesh on December 16, Randhir Jaiswal said: “This is a matter between the former prime minister and the Bangladesh government. We have nothing more to say about it.”
Regarding the extradition request for Sheikh Hasina, he said: “The extradition request is being examined according to our established procedure (prevailing rules). However, the matter of any citizen who wishes to return to their country voluntarily, including with travel documents, is separate from the extradition request.”
Regarding the deterioration of the law and order situation in Bangladesh and allegations of attacks on Hindus, he said: “We are concerned about incidents of violence against minorities in Bangladesh. We urge the Bangladesh government to conduct thorough investigations into these incidents and bring the perpetrators to justice.”
Meanwhile, citing a person named Syed Mozammel Ali, who identifies himself as Sheikh Hasina’s spokesperson, a Reuters report published on Tuesday (November 24) said that ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina wants to return to Bangladesh on December 16, Victory Day.
After spending more than 2 years in exile in India, she has urged the government to arrange an aircraft of the state-flag carrier Biman Bangladesh Airlines for her return to the country.

item.title: New Bank Company Act draft curbs family, political control on boards
item.description:
The government is moving to curtail the opportunity for a single family to maintain control over a bank.
The scope for securing a spot on a bank’s board through political identity is also shrinking.
Under the new provisions, initiatives are being taken to establish a structure where no more than two members from a single family can serve as directors of a bank.
Furthermore, the doors to bank boards and top management are closing for ministers, members of parliament, and local government representatives.
A director's tenure is also being limited once again; as part of this process, a proposal has been made to reduce a director's consecutive term from the current 12 years down to 6 years.
These changes have been introduced in the draft amendment to the Bank Company Act, 1991.
The Ministry of Finance has already finalized the draft. It also proposes several new provisions regarding bank ownership, the composition of the board of directors, the appointment of directors, and loan recovery rules.
Relevant responsible sources have confirmed this information.
Declining dominance of family and politics
Currently, a maximum of three members from a single family can serve as directors of a bank.
In the final draft amendment to the Bank Company Act, 1991, this number will be reduced to two.
Representation on the board through institutions owned or controlled by the same family is also being curtailed, with a proposal to allow only one representative instead of the current maximum of two from such entities.
Direct bans are also being introduced to curb political influence on boards.
According to the new provisions, cabinet members, individuals holding government positions of equivalent rank, members of parliament, and local government representatives will be barred from becoming directors of any bank.
Similarly, none of them will be eligible to become a bank’s Managing Director (MD) or Chief Executive Officer (CEO).
Those who become directors will not be allowed to serve for more than six consecutive years.
Anyone wishing to become a director again will have to observe a three-year cooling-off period.
Additionally, loan defaulters, individuals convicted of criminal offenses, those involved in financial irregularities, or anyone who has violated regulatory rules will remain ineligible to become directors.
Individuals without at least 10 years of experience in the relevant field will also not be eligible.
The draft proposes retaining the existing provisions in these areas.
In 2018, the tenure of directors was extended from six years to nine years, and in 2023, it was further increased to 12 years.
The new proposal calls for returning to the six-year limit.
Number of independent directors to increase
A proposal has been made to increase the number of independent directors on bank boards.
Currently, a 20-member board is required to have at least three independent directors; under the new rules, this number will rise to four.
For boards with fewer than 20 members, there must be at least three independent directors, up from the current two.
Stricter rules are also coming for appointing independent directors: anyone who has been associated with or had a conflict of interest with the respective bank or its affiliated institutions within the past three years cannot be appointed as an independent director.
Meanwhile, the existing cap prohibiting an individual, company, or family—either singly or jointly—from holding more than 10% of a bank's shares will remain unchanged.
However, there is a proposal to grant Bangladesh Bank the authority to relax this limit for strategic investors under special circumstances.
New measures to recover loans from directors
The revised final draft law proposes adding a provision to surrender shares to recover dues owed to the bank if a director's position falls vacant.
If loan dues remain unpaid even after surrendering shares, they can be recovered as public demands under the Public Demands Recovery Act, 1913.
There is also a proposal to close off opportunities to regularize such loans through rescheduling or other means—meaning the scope to evade loan repayment liabilities after losing a directorship will be further restricted.
Moreover, no director will be allowed to remain absent from board meetings for more than three consecutive months without the board's approval, nor will they be permitted to take such leave more than once a year.
Setting time limits after board dissolution
Proposals have been made to further clarify who will manage a bank and for how long if Bangladesh Bank dissolves its board of directors.
In this regard, the two-year limit for the board dissolution order will remain intact.
However, individuals appointed by the central bank will serve for the tenure specified in their appointment letters, with their total tenure—including extensions—not exceeding three years.
Afterward, shareholders will elect new directors at the Annual General Meeting (AGM).
There is also a proposal to empower Bangladesh Bank to waive, cancel, or reduce penalties if a bank fails to maintain statutory cash and liquid asset requirements during restructuring, merger, liquidation, or acquisition, subject to the approval of the central bank's board of directors.
Higher fines for violating the law
Financial penalties for violating provisions of the Bank Company Act are also being increased.
For failing to provide necessary information or documents, or for disobeying various provisions of the law, the minimum fine is proposed to be raised from Tk20,000 to Tk50,000.
Additionally, if a bank wishes to amend its Memorandum or Articles of Association, it must first obtain a No Objection Certificate (NOC) from Bangladesh Bank, for which a new section has been proposed in the law.
The draft also broadens the definition of "affiliated institutions."
Relationships such as sitting on an institution's board of directors, holding more than 20% of its shares, or acting as a loan guarantor will be considered grounds for affiliation.
Furthermore, the existing definition of a loan defaulter—where a loan remains unpaid for more than six months—has been retained.
